items.headline: Goalkeeper Malagón Out with ACL Tear
items.body: <cite index="6-2">Luis Ángel Malagón, expected to start in net for Mexico, suffered a torn ACL early in the year and will miss the tournament.</cite> <cite index="6-8">This saw Guillermo Ochoa back into the national team fold after the program had seemingly moved on from the 40-year-old legend.</cite>

items.headline: Ochoa Confirmed for Record Sixth World Cup
items.body: <cite index="11-21">Evergreen goalkeeper Guillermo Ochoa could feature in his sixth World Cup campaign.</cite> <cite index="6-23,6-24">Ochoa, age 40, is set to take part in a record sixth World Cup, level with Cristiano Ronaldo.</cite>

items.headline: Lozano & Huescas Excluded Due to Fitness
items.body: <cite index="5-1">Hirving Lozano was left out because of disciplinary issues and limited playing time with San Diego FC.</cite> <cite index="5-2">Rodrigo Huescas was excluded as he continues recovering from a serious knee injury.</cite>

items.headline: Returning Players Being Monitored
items.body: <cite index="5-8">Aguirre decided to monitor several players returning from injuries, including Luis Chávez, César Huerta, Julián Araujo, and captain Edson Álvarez, who is expected to be one of the emotional and tactical leaders of the squad.</cite>

items.headline: Strong Pre-Tournament Run
items.body: <cite index="10-1,10-2">Mexico have been in strong form recently, winning 3 of their last 5 matches (60% win rate), scoring 9 goals and conceding 2 during this period.</cite>

items.headline: Recent Competitive Success
items.body: <cite index="6-25,6-26">Under Javier Aguirre's third spell, Mexico led them to victory in the 2024/25 CONCACAF Nations League and then led Mexico to the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup crown, beating the U.S. in the final.</cite>

items.headline: Home Advantage Expectations
items.body: <cite index="11-4">After quarter-final finishes at the home editions in 1970 and 1986, Mexico arrive at this year's global football showpiece, hoping to replicate the success of their 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup campaign.</cite>

items.headline: Opening Match vs South Africa
items.body: <cite index="22-1">Thursday, June 11: Group A: Mexico vs. South Africa (Mexico City), 1 p.m. local / 3 p.m. ET.</cite> <cite index="18-15,18-16">The two teams have faced each other four times, most recently in a 1–1 draw in the 2010 FIFA World Cup opening match, with South Africa as the host nation. This match will take place exactly 16 years after.</cite>

items.headline: Second Match vs South Korea
items.body: <cite index="7-22">Mexico then face South Korea on June 18 in Guadalajara.</cite> <cite index="18-19">The teams have played three times, most recently in a 2016 friendly, a 2–1 victory for the South Koreans.</cite>

items.headline: Final Group Match vs Czechia
items.body: <cite index="7-22">Mexico face Czechia on June 24 in Mexico City.</cite> <cite index="18-23,18-25">Mexico and Czechia have met 15 times including twice in the World Cup, with Mexico winning both matches: 3–1 in the 1998 tournament in France, and 2–1 in the 2018 edition in Russia.</cite>

items.headline: Veteran Striker Jiménez in Prime Form
items.body: <cite index="11-19,11-20">All eyes will be on Mexico's hero and veteran striker, Raúl Jiménez. The 34-year-old arrives at his home World Cup after a strong season with Premier League club Fulham, in which he reached double digits in the scoring charts.</cite>

items.headline: Captain Edson Álvarez as Tactical Leader
items.body: <cite index="6-9">Experienced midfielder Edson Alvarez has been included on the roster, having only just barely returned from ankle surgery before the end of the club season.</cite> He anchors the midfield and leadership structure.

items.headline: Midfield Depth & Experience
items.body: <cite index="11-21">Mexico have abundance of talent in young midfielders Gilberto Mora and Obed Vargas.</cite> <cite index="6-23">With five players in the squad who have at least 90 international appearances and nine more with at least 40, Mexico relies heavily on experience.</cite>

items.headline: Pressure of Home Hosting
items.body: <cite index="5-9,5-10,5-11">Mexico is preparing for one of the biggest moments in its football history. The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be hosted by Mexico, the United States and Canada, and El Tri hopes home-field advantage can help deliver a historic run. Mexico will once again try to use the energy of its fans to reach at least the quarterfinals, a stage the national team has only achieved when hosting the World Cup in 1970 and 1986.</cite>

items.headline: Betting Odds & Realistic Ceiling
items.body: <cite index="7-2,7-3">Mexico are long shots to win the tournament despite home advantage, sitting well down the outright board behind the European and South American contenders. Prices range from around 67.00 to 81.00 in decimal, a sign of how differently sportsbooks weigh a home run against the squad's ceiling.</cite>

items.headline: Group A Scenario
items.body: <cite index="18-2">The group consists of Mexico (co-host), South Africa, South Korea, and Czechia.</cite> <cite index="21-2">Mexico has not reached a World Cup quarterfinal since 1986 when current manager Javier Aguirre was playing on the team.</cite>
